task: round11 RE-CHECK OLD CONCLUSIONS (3 closed/rejected ideas vs new facts)
summary: Round 11 recheck, 26 Sep ~17:10-18:10 UTC. It takes three conclusions that rounds 2-10 did not re-check, chosen for the round's successor-scenario focus and the tie rule. Skipped as already covered: everything in the round 2-10 skip lists (floatout ... I-146, finetuned primary, I-209). (A) The E10 rule's exclusion P6, 'no successor + insertion build, no C10 rider path (new code after R8, unscored stack)', is PARTLY OVERTURNED. Its 'new code' reason is mostly wrong: the K2 patch set (divinsert, lowrefine, safetail) applies in memory with every anchor exactly once, and every cell compiles, on all three x138-family notebooks on disk: Harmonic Fusion V3, amanatar v1 and amanatar v10, whose post cell differs from x138's by up to 1,169 lines. In all three, linefit is the last graph edit, so the insertion slot is unchanged. The scan_hyp_successor agent found the same independently. The missing code is only a sha-pinned successor entry in BASES. The 'unscored stack' reason is weakened: the insertion gained +0.001 public on 3 of 3 stacks (#27->#28, #34->#35, #38->#37). Two real risks remain. First, a successor that changes the division stage (the private 'x138-s3forks' name hints at this) makes the insertion's marginal value unknown. Second, a deadline trade-off: the safetail recipe replaces the successor's 27000 s repair guard with 34200 s, while the #35 recipe keeps the guard but lets late clips lose their safe divisions and linefit under x138's own degrade when runtime nears 7.5 h. Verdict: revive as contingency tooling plus a pre-registered clause for E10 v2 (user OK needed); never a port by itself. (B) ILP division weight / ILP forks (v3 s_merge, 'upheld: exp12 precision 0.19 < 0.265') STAYS CLOSED, but its stated reason was wrong twice. The 0.19 belongs to weight 0.6, while x138 runs 1.2, which gives 36/241 = 0.149 in-sample. The 0.265 break-even is also superseded. NEW FACT: the break-even for any further division-add on top of K2 is 0.161 on the lab (J after insertion 25/130 = 0.192), not round 8's 0.114, which was pre-insertion. The idea fails on in-sample precision below 0.161, no output channel (x138 relink is one-to-one) and no bed (the exp60 edge_cache holds 0 ILP edges). (C) '#34 (x138 byte copy) as a final / never tick exp56' STAYS CLOSED, re-derived under the tie rule. #34 (submitted ~08:09 UTC 25 Sep, behind ~240 earlier copies) would rank ~450-640 on private at exactly X, beyond bronze (~395) in essentially every world. It would also give up the twin's world 'insertion < 0 and lowrefine > 0', where the twin sits above all ~350 copies. Finals stay #37 + #38. Nothing was submitted, pushed or committed. Only the round-11 scan_recheck files were written. The anchor test ran in memory from the scratchpad.

Under the tie rule a late verbatim port sits at the bottom of its copy block, while successor+insertion sits above or below ALL of its copies by the insertion's sign. (2) MEASURED (scratchpad anchor_test.py, in memory, writes nothing): with x138's cell indices (config 2 / predict 4 / post 5), the patches divinsert, lowrefine and safetail, alone and together, apply with every anchor count == 1, and every cell compiles, on x138 (control), Harmonic Fusion V3 (md5 76a4f419), amanatar v1 (3ce943d4) and amanatar v10 (24ecb611). In all four, the line after linefit_smooth_output_graph is the FINAL print and the return, so the insertion stays the last graph edit. (3) LB record of the insertion: +0.001 on 3 of 3 stacks (probe 27 0.947 -> 28 0.948; #34 0.953 -> #35 0.954; #38 0.953 -> #37 0.954). The x138 pairs share the public embryo, so this is one embryo twice plus one older stack. NEW VERDICT: PARTLY REVIVED as contingency. 'New code' shrinks to a sha-pinned BASES entry for the successor plus an assertion that linefit is followed directly by FINAL/return; the patch code is unchanged. 'Unscored stack' becomes a gate question, not a ban. Remaining real risks: (a) a successor whose diff touches safe-division, linefit or fork code: the insertion's marginal value is then unknown, and DIVINS_STEAL may fight the successor's forks; (b) the deadline trade-off (see R11-PI-deadline-recipe); (c) one shot, with no lab parity on the successor.

findings.action: Main session / round-11 report: put 'successor + insertion' into the E10 v2 draft as a gated option. It is not a ban, and it never replaces the verbatim rule without the user's separate OK. Gate text to pre-register BEFORE any trigger: (1) successor sha pinned, 12 code cells with the x138 layout, every patch anchor count == 1 (the builder already asserts this); (2) the successor's diff vs x138 touches no safe-division, fork or DIVINS-name code (grep add_safe_divisions / fork / daughter in the diff = 0 new lines); otherwise successor + insertion is not built; (3) the dummy rebuild of K2/twin stays byte-identical (sha 1f1ddb6d / 55038fd6); (4) the insertion's fail-soft line in the dummy log. Coordinate with scan_hyp_successor, which holds the same anchor result; do not double-count it.

findings.what: Which insertion recipe to use on a successor has no good default. (i) The K1/K2 recipe (--patch safetail) is refused by the builder unless REPAIR_DEADLINE_S is 34200 or 37800. That replaces the successor's own 27000 s guard, so the output is no longer 'successor + insertion only' whenever the successor's runtime passes 7.5 h. (ii) The #35 recipe (divinsert only) keeps the 27000 s guard. But the insertion adds runtime before later clips' repair (#35 L (6.72, 7.73] h vs #34 <= 6.46 h; K2 - twin <= 0.85 h), so on a successor slower than x138, late clips can hit x138's degrade path, which drops safe divisions and linefit (the reason safetail exists: BIOHUB_DEGRADE_KEEP_DIV). A successor's hidden runtime is unknown until it is scored.
findings.evidence: tools/build_probe_kernel.py patch_safetail docstring (l.1464-1471) and main() refusal of other deadlines (CONTEXT 26 Sep 04:12 UTC); CONTEXT 25 Sep 14:05 UTC (T1 SAFETAIL); RESULTS.md #34/#35 latencies; CONTEXT 26 Sep 07:35 UTC (insertion runtime <= 0.85 h).
findings.action: Decide in the E10 v2 draft, before any trigger, one mechanical rule. Example: use recipe (ii) only if the successor author's own logged runtime + 1.0 h <= 7.0 h; otherwise use recipe (i) with 34200 and label the file 'successor + insertion + safetail'. Do not improvise this at trigger time.

findings.what: ILP division weight / using ILP forks (probe 3, v3 FINAL_REPORT §j-18, s_merge.json 'upheld: exp12 ILP forks 24 TP / 103 FP = 0.19 precision, below the 0.265 break-even'). WHAT CHANGED: round 8 superseded the 0.265 public break-even (lab 0.114 / private 0.11-0.20), which on its face would put 0.19 above break-even. RE-DERIVED: (1) The 0.19 is exp12 at weight 0.6. x138 runs BIOHUB_ILP_DIVISION_WEIGHT = 1.2, where exp12 gave 36 TP / 205 FP = 0.149. Both numbers are in-sample, because the pilkwang weights saw all train videos. (2) The break-even that applies to anything added on top of K2 is J/(1+J) with J AFTER the insertion: exp60 ins35 pooled TP/FP/FN 25/31/74, J = 0.192, q* = 0.161. Round 8's 0.114 was the pre-insertion control. (3) The marginal precision over safe divisions + insertion is below the raw 0.149, and a fork FP also costs an evaluable edge. (4) There is no channel: x138's relink is one-to-one and emits no ILP forks (§j-14). (5) There is no bed: the exp60 edge_cache npz files hold 0 ILP edges, so it cannot be replayed. NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED, with the reason corrected (in-sample 0.149 < 0.161, no channel, no bed, R8).

findings.what: The division-add break-even on top of the K2 stack is q* = J/(1+J) = 0.161 on the exp60 lab (ins35 pooled 25 TP / 31 FP / 74 FN, J 0.192). Round 8's 0.114 describes the pre-insertion control (16/25/83). One division TP is worth ~0.1*(1+J)/U = 9.2e-4 lab against ~7.4e-6 for one edge flip, so the division term dominates any fork rider. The private break-even range 0.11-0.20 should now be read at its upper half for riders stacked on the insertion, or on a successor + insertion.

findings.action: Use 0.161 (not 0.114) in any post-deadline division-add gate on the K2 stack. Record it in KNOWLEDGE next to I-079.
